tier_reason: C stands only on upstream issue #239 (same machine, cold and warm runs measured against no cache); the OpenMW MR !5021 numbers alone are D-grade: no measured uncached time, separate pipelines, extra build-setting changes only in the cached config, and a fork rather than upstream.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Upstream issue #239 (one user's build, 4-core 2 GHz machine with SSD): 4:49 without clcache, 6:22 with a cold cache (slower) and 2:06 with a warm cache, about 2.3x on the warm rebuild (derived from page data). OpenMW MR !5021 (Aussiemon fork, commit 21c50c2) reports CI jobs dropping from near the 2-hour timeout to 55 and 49 minutes, but the uncached time is never measured.
corrections.hardware: Issue #239: 4-core 2 GHz machine with an SSD (CPU model not given).
corrections.workload: Issue #239: one MSVC project built without clcache, with an empty cache and with a warm cache on the same machine. Secondary: OpenMW GitLab CI job (MSBuild, MSVC 2022, 64-bit RelWithDebInfo) uncached versus a clcache fork with a CI-restored cache.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: in MR !5021 only the cached configuration sets PRECOMPILE_HEADERS_WITH_MSVC=OFF (OpenMW defaults to ON), rewrites /Zi to /Z7 and sets /p:TrackFileAccess=false, and the runs are separate pipelines. Cold builds are slower than no cache (#239; 7 to 23 minutes in #251); lock timeouts (#251, #347) remain open; /Zi and PCH compiles are not cached; the compiler hash uses only cl.exe mtime and size; upstream lacks Python 3.10+ and /external:I support.

Enricher: the cross-run gap exceeds the spread (four other uncached main runs spent 763-1,062 s in the doc-review step, against 384 s and 168 s with sccache), PR #1571 also moved the toolchain and rust-cache steps ahead of the measured build, and the 85% C/C++ hit rate came from objects main's clippy step had already cached. Preprocessor cache mode (PR #1882) works only with GCC/Clang on local disk, so MSVC and remote backends preprocess on every lookup; issue #160 (closed in 2024 without new timings) is the only ccache comparison, so there is no evidence sccache beats ccache. Open issue #2821: the GitHub Actions cache backend silently drops writes on HTTP 429 (45-90% loss with concurrent writers), matching the PR's 219 write errors. MSVC /Yc, /Fp and shared PDBs are not cacheable.
